content.jointProblem: Can product-description embeddings and category metadata, optionally combined with sparse purchase signals, produce more useful product-page recommendations than best-seller sorting for one Harmat client with only 500–2,000 transactions? The first experiment would test transfer from text retrieval to product recommendation by comparing content-based and lightweight hybrid methods against best-seller and category-based baselines using time-separated purchase data and a small, human-reviewed relevance set.

rationale.text: Petrović has demonstrated sentence-embedding development and comparative evaluation expertise relevant to testing semantic similarity between product descriptions.

sources.quote: we perform a systematic comparison of twelve sentence encoder variants
We release the benchmark, trained models, and evaluation toolkit.

rationale.text: His retrieval research provides experience comparing dense retrieval with lexical and multilingual baselines, useful for designing a controlled recommendation prototype rather than assuming embeddings will help.

sources.quote: We fine-tune a bi-encoder retrieval model initialised from a Serbian transformer checkpoint and compare it against BM25, a multilingual DPR baseline, and a cross-encoder re-ranker.

rationale.text: His cross-script embedding work is relevant if the selected catalogue contains Serbian descriptions in both Latin and Cyrillic scripts.

sources.quote: This paper proposes a script-unified embedding approach that maps Latin-script and Cyrillic-script Serbian sentences to a shared vector space.

rationale.text: A joint project is consistent with his stated participation preferences.

sources.quote: He is open to industrial PhD supervision and joint research projects with companies seeking NLP solutions.

constraints.text: The approach must work with the existing sparse transaction history rather than depend on collecting a substantially larger dataset.

sources.quote: The largest dataset had 1 900 completed orders over eighteen months; the smallest had around 520.
We do not have the budget or the traffic to wait for larger datasets.

constraints.text: Best-seller sorting must remain an explicit evaluation baseline, and the initial deliverable should be limited to a prototype for one client.

sources.quote: Simple best-seller sorting actually outperformed the model in our A/B test on the one client where we got far enough to test.
A working prototype for one client would be enough to start.

constraints.text: Data access must use anonymised transaction and catalogue data under an agreed data-sharing arrangement; the actual fields and permitted uses need confirmation.

sources.quote: We can give a collaborator full read access to anonymised transaction and product catalogue data.
access to anonymised client datasets under a data-sharing agreement.

constraints.text: Company-side implementation and review must fit roughly one developer-day per week.

sources.quote: We can allocate one mid-level developer for roughly one day per week to an applied research collaboration

constraints.text: The prototype integration should accommodate the company's existing e-commerce and deployment environment; available serving resources and latency limits remain to be established.

sources.quote: WooCommerce and custom REST API integrations
Docker for containerised deployments on client VPS environments

risks: The supplied research demonstrates text similarity, retrieval and other NLP tasks, not transaction-sparse recommendation. Similar descriptions may identify substitutes rather than useful complementary purchases; the first experiment must explicitly test that transfer gap.
The strongest evidence concerns Serbian. Catalogue languages are unknown, and performance on Hungarian or Slovak product text is not established by the supplied material.
Sparse purchases and low traffic may make both offline estimates and online uplift inconclusive. Human relevance judgments can diagnose errors but cannot establish increased sales.

Catalogue description quality, category consistency, impression logging and historical inventory availability are unknown; missing information could undermine either content-based recommendations or unbiased evaluation.
Researcher availability, project duration, total budget and deployment resources are unknown. Limited company engineering capacity could delay integration even if offline results are promising.
questions: Can Petrović confirm availability, proposed effort and a feasible timetable for a joint project, and what budget can Harmat commit?
Which client will supply the first dataset, and what are its catalogue size, languages, scripts, description coverage and category quality?

Do the anonymised exports retain order timestamps and line items, and are product-view, recommendation-impression, click and historical availability records accessible under the data-sharing agreement?

Should the widget recommend substitutes, complementary products or both? What relevance criteria, offline metrics and minimum commercially meaningful improvement over best-seller sorting should be agreed before testing?

Can the first experiment compare lexical/category matching, multilingual and Serbian embeddings where applicable, and a lightweight hybrid on time-separated data, with human review specifically checking whether semantic similarity transfers to useful recommendations?
What VPS resources, response-time limits, integration responsibilities, model licensing requirements and online testing window apply to the selected client?
